[2023-12-17 10:03] koalaman18 : While I'm a veteran, I don't consider myself a very good player of the game 😂 I do think that's part and parcel of FTP, though - people can pick and choose which parts of the game to focus on, and they will tend to get an advantage in those areas at the expense of not competing in others, whereas people who try to do everything will find things tougher. Another example is as Crowie said earlier - many managers focus on SOD but use T20 to get extra experience into their younger players. I don't do this, I try to compete in both formats, hence my best players tend to be lower in experience which does hurt you in FTP.  Quite a few of the recent changes have been us trying to make sure that these sort of advantages gotten from ignoring one format or facet are not insurmountable. Examples including combining the youth and senior academies, and increasing the wage discount for home-grown players (giving home-grown clubs a financial boost compared to heavy TM users). But still those advantages will exist, and there isn't really any getting away from that fact.

[2024-02-27 14:27] koalaman18 : Apart from a seriously good and interesting FC engine (unlike Battrick's which is... substandard) the main point of difference for CC was that your tactics were extremely customisable. You could tell your batters or bowlers to play more aggressively/defensively depending on things like the team or individual score, how many overs had passed, how long there was left in the session, and so on. That would create tactical decisions similar to real cricket such as when to declare or whether to chase a target or settle for a draw. The pitch and weather also changed as the game went on and played a real role - you did not want to be caught batting last on a wearing pitch.  The tactics could be too complex for some people, but personally I loved it. The rest of the game was very simple: only four skills for each player (batting, bowling, fielding, keeping), very basic training and finances, and youth recruitment was essentially automated. It was the matches themselves and the strategic battle with the other manager that made the game fun, and as a small-scale game (a few hundred teams at its most popular) you'd often end up facing the same teams and forming rivalries. The creator ultimately didn't end up having the time or money to keep supporting it, though, so it shut down in late 2022. I still miss it, probably my favourite game I've played.

[2024-05-16 13:49] crowfan65 : what do you think made it the best
[2024-05-16 14:40] mike778 : All players have their own set of skills and traits and as a manager you have to figure out the best way to use them.  FTP has a bit of that with talents but still suffers from the clone builds where all players are trained to pretty much the same model.  Stumped also nailed the player ageing model. Players peaked around 25 but their longer peak period was around 22-28.  There isn't the dead period FTP has where players aren't much use early 20s.
[2024-05-16 14:55] koalaman18 : It's funny to see Stumped's player ageing praised given I remember there being overwhelming criticism of it at times - people getting upset that players in their mid-20s were already on the decline.  I strongly agree with the player skill sets being what set Stumped apart. In particular the separation of batters' (shot selection/attack/defence) and bowlers' (accuracy/movement/variation) skills, and the use of potentials to limit the maximum a player could reach in each skill. You could get a slogger who couldn't play a defensive shot, or a bowler who hooped it around corners but was cannon fodder if the ball wasn't moving. And you would have to build a strategy around the players you had, and/or search for missing links on the transfer market.  I think this also contributed to players being useful as soon as they graduated your DEV team at the age of 22. They might not be at their peak yet, and inexperienced, but normally they were already really good at what their "best" skill or role in the side was, so you could find a place for them in your side.
[2024-05-16 15:08] alphabull88 : Variety in terms of players especially batsman would be a great addition to ftp
[2024-05-16 16:50] .notaknot : In terms of batter diversity - I'm curious whether people prefer trainable diversity (e.g. batters trained to be high strength will do particularly well on e.g. slow and sticky pitches and batters with especially high batting will do particularly well on e.g. flat and hard pitches) or non-trainable diversity (e.g. mediums do better on green; spinners do better on dry - regardless of how they are trained. And any talents).
[2024-05-16 16:51] .notaknot : It sounds like stumps advantage here is in trainable, and I guess non-trainable is easier to do. But I haven't played stumped so I'm not sure how accurate my interpretation of what people wrote is
[2024-05-16 17:08] alphabull88 : A combination training plus natural ability. Stumped and battrick both have 5 levels of aggression for a batter 1 being very defensive to 5 being very aggressive. This can be a great addition.
[2024-05-16 17:10] alphabull88 : Batsmans strike rate will then depend not only on his skills but also his mentality or play style
[2024-05-16 17:35] mike778 : Stumped player diversity  came from potential.  Training was just a way of reaching that potential. You can't make someone what they aren't   Eg.  If a player had  6 potential fielding 20 potential variations  20 potential accuracy  4 potential movement  Then they will always be a very bad fielder, there is nothing you can do about it from a training perspective.  They can be an incredible death bowler.  But largely ineffective with the new ball. From a training perspective you are trying to turn them into that demon death bowler.  They also have characteristics which are a bit more specialised than FTP talents such as partnership breaker, superstar, bullet arm and so on.  And you end up with a player who has their own se t of strengths and weaknesses different to pretty much every other player.  The downside though is from a training point of view, you have fewer options to make the player how you want them.  But generally in most games where you have that option you end up with clones using the optimal model.
[2024-05-16 18:29] .notaknot : What would you expect/want to happen if an instinctively defensive player is asked to play aggressively, or an instinctively aggressive player is asked to play defensively? Would they cancel or is are there potential subtleties?

[2024-05-17 01:11] koalaman18 : I do think the greater complexity was a factor holding Stumped back sadly. I think the low user base is an underestimated factor in why the dev activity stopped and the game is now shutting down - Stumped wasn't bringing in money, so the devs have to work full-time in real life and that along with family commitments left no time or resources to run the game. [2024-05-17 01:23] koalaman18 : My experience was that they'd cancel, at least in terms of the player's intentions. [2024-06-30 05:47] .notaknot : A useful trick, if expecting to win and trying to maximise NRR, is to figure out if you expect your batting to be faster or slower than your current "for" speed. This will not only depend on opposition but also e.g. pitch/weather conditions.  The point is that (if you win) you will bat more overs (which will weight the game higher in the NRR calculations) if you bat first. So if it's e.g. sticky against an average opponent it might be better to minimise the "damage" by batting 2nd, and if it's e.g. flat against the weakest team in the league it might be better to bat 1st to maximise the NRR gain.  Of course making sure you win is still the most important thing. This is just an extra trick if you're struggling to make up a NRR shortfall

[2024-07-16 03:42] savio4315 : I think before finding ways to bring teams out of debt, we need to find ways to prevent new teams from getting into debt in the first place.  Whenever the manager is trying to purchase a new player or orders an upgrade to stadium or academy, it would be helpful if the game could flash a warning about the impact that decision could have on their finances. So you could identify what is the budget of the team based on the current sponsorship and average gates for the team and other teams in the division. And maybe set the warning at about 90% of this budget. So if the purchase or upgrade is likely to go over 90% of the budget then you warn the manager of the consequences.  You could also provide a metric of how many weeks will the team take to get into debt if they already have a positive balance.  Also at the start of a new season which is when wages increase and maybe even sponsorship/gates income might increase or decrease based on promotion/demotion then at that point you can again provide a warning if the new income to expense ratio puts the team on the path to getting into debt.  Doing things like this should hopefully prevent any new teams from getting into debt in the first place.

[2024-11-10 16:50] casperj_ftp : Depends on what your finances look like. The main issue with upgrading is often the increase in weekly running costs. At the start of the season your players' wages get recalculated as well (normally they'll increase) so you can get caught out  in terms of balancing your finances at the start of the season. I'd wait a couple of weeks into the season and see how your profit/loss values are each week. Based on that, if you think you can afford the extra weekly amount for the next academy level then go for it!

[2025-01-12 10:44] jujoh_24730 : The discussion in the TM topic got me thinking about how to make 21-23 yo players more attractive. The main issue is that you can't keep them without playing them, since they will lag behind on experience and that is vital. So four options to increase experience on these players: 1. Send then out on loan. Doing this via the TM is probably too big a risk for the game integrity. How about having the option to send a player on a fictional loan period for one season during this age span. You can't play the player for 15 weeks, but pay (most if not all of) his wages in return for an experience gain of say 14 div 4 SOD games. Possibly these players can be picked up on loan by other teams but the mechanics should not be intertwined.  2. Play in second XI. Which is what happens irl. They get a fatigue hit as if they play an intense game and an experience gain that is about 75% of a div 4 SOD game. You can play them in senior games but the fatigue will add up. 3. Act as twelfth man. One 21-23 yo player can be selected each week to be twelfth man. He gets a slight fatigue hit and a slight experience gain. 4. Diminishing experience gains as players age. This would not change a lot for the big teams but it opens up the senior farm strategy and will encourage teams to play more youngsters.  All in all it would be best to have changes in performance for younger players alongside this. They should be able to perform as good as 30yos when they are 23, but maybe not in every game.  Disclaimer: I understand that without coders none of this will be implemented anytime soon.

[2025-06-10 10:19] powerbug96 : I just want to get in ahead of the comments which will come regarding the latest news item. Please read that if you haven't already.  Fitness updates have been brought forward 16 hours. So what previously ran on Sunday at 19:00 for NZ *was* going to run at Sunday 03:00 under the initial proposal. This meant if a NZ side played a cup game away (even if it was in Aus) then their players would only have 1 fitness update between finishing MKMC and playing ST20. Right now it's two. This would be a big problem with the way players recover in fatigue. Additionally problem would occur for pretty much any away MKMC match in a time zone later than your home time, only the Canadian league sides would be guaranteed to have no impact to their fatigue.  This decision to skip the Sunday update and double up on Monday is where we've landed for S62. It will not make any difference to your senior players I want that to be clear. You change will be that between YT20 and YOD there is now 4 updates, and only 3 between YOD and YT20. Previously was it 3 then 4. Your actual difference will come from youths who play MKMC and then YT20 the next day, there's no fatigue update between those two games.  Please note this is a trial period regarding these changes. We wanted to bring these updates forward to give people more time between the updates and their matches, and this is still the case overall.

You will get better ticket prices in the higher division but if you are getting caned every week your supporter mood will suffer and you will get less supporters join your club.  In the lower division you get lesser ticket prices but if you keep winning you probably get higher crowds, higher supporter mood, which leads to higher crowds....
